sections.skill: Check subtitles and translated audio for timing, meaning and names

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: What are subtitles?

choices.text: Spoken words shown as text on screen
A voice in a second language that replaces the speaker's voice in the original video

questions.correct_answer: Spoken words shown as text on screen
questions.intro: SUBTITLES show spoken words as text on screen; generated subtitles come from transcription and sometimes translation. TRANSLATED AUDIO, or AI DUBBING, replaces speech with a voice in another language. Check three things. TIMING: does each line appear when it is spoken and stay long enough to read? MEANING: is the translation faithful, or did an idiom such as "break a leg" become nonsense? NAMES AND TERMS: are people, places and technical words right? A fluent-sounding dub can still change meaning, so a speaker of both languages should review anything important.

sections.skill: Check a subtitle line with three questions

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: The subtitle appears two seconds late. Which check fails?

choices.text: Meaning, because a late subtitle always means that the words were translated wrongly

questions.intro: For each subtitle line ask three questions. TIMING: does it appear when the words are spoken and stay at least long enough to read (often about one second per few words)? MEANING: does it say what the speaker meant, not just a word-for-word copy? NAMES: are names and terms spelled correctly? Example: a speaker says "Dr. Nguyen, it's raining cats and dogs," and the subtitle reads "Dr. Wen, many animals are falling," two seconds late. All three checks fail.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Handle tone, consent and disclosure in translated media

questions.domain: Creative: audio, music, video and synthetic media
questions.prompt: A polite request in the original became a rude command in the dub. What changed?
questions.intro: Translation can shift tone and politeness as well as words: a friendly phrase may become rude, or a formal one too casual. Jokes, numbers and units (miles versus kilometers) need care. Dubbed voices that imitate the original speaker raise consent questions. When you publish translated media, say that subtitles or audio were machine-generated if a human did not fully review them, and give viewers a way to report errors.
